get.description: AccountQuery is a list query that returns data for all accounts that match the provided filter criteria. Notice that it returns only data internal to the account itself. It doesn’t return any data about transactions involving the account. It does, however, return the parent account, if there is one. You can search across all accounts or you can specify an account type and search only those. If you are querying for an account whose FullName contains a number, the query might return an account that has a matching account number rather than a matching FullName. For example, if you are querying for an account named 12345, and 12345 happens to be the account number of a totally different account, the query won’t return what you asked for (the account named 12345), but instead will return the account with the account number 12345. This problem won’t happen if: the “show account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, or the account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 12345a.

post.description: This message allows you to perform the same activities as a user does in the QB New Account form, which can be accessed in QB by selecting Lists->Chart of Accounts->Accounts->New. If you want the account to be a subaccount to an existing account, similar to using the SubAccount checkbox and selection list drop down in the New Account form, you use the ParentRef aggregate. Notice that the ParentRef can take either the parent account’s ListID or FullName. It is important to note that the parent account specified in the ParentRef must have the same account type (AccountType) of the child account that you are creating. (The AccountType field maps to the Type pulldown menu in the New Accounts field.) The AccountNumber is NOT the account number assigned by your bank or other entity. (That number is specified in the BankNumber field.) The account number is simply part of a numbering scheme used by accounting systems to help provide a visual hierarchy and ordering of all of the accounts in a Chart of Accounts. QuickBooks provides this functionality for those who need or want it, but by default has this functionality turned off. The AccountNumber field maps to the Number field in the New Account form, which appears only if the Accounting preferences for the company have been set to use account numbering. By default, account numbers aren’t used. In the SDK, you can set the account numbers if you want, even if the preference for it has been turned off. The numbers would then appear later if the user turned this preference on. In the OpenBalance field for certain types of new Accounts, you may want to leave the opening balance at 0 if you are going to fund the account from another account. That process will effectively create the opening balance. How do you increase and decrease amounts in bank accounts? The following requests increase the balance in a bank account: Deposit Add ReceivePaymentAdd Journal Entry Add Sales ReceiptAdd The following requests decrease the balance in a bank account: CheckAdd Bill PaymentCheckAdd JournalEntryAdd The `account_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

get.description: Returns employee data. Notice that prior to qbXML spec 4.0, an EmployeeQueryRq would return a permissions error if the currently logged in QuickBooks user didn’t have “Payroll and Employees” permission. This would occur even if you only needed data that wasn’t restricted. However, because of IncludeRetElement (beginning with qbXML spec 4.0), the situation has changed somewhat. You can use that new element to specify fields in the EmployeeRet object that don’t require “Payroll and Employees” permissions. Such a query would return the unrestricted data (such as Name) from an EmployeeQueryRq even if the logged in user lacks “Payroll and Employees” permissions.

parameters.description: Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a. response_json.description: `null` until answered. Then QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer, in one of the two shapes below.

account_ref.description: AccountRef points to an account in the company file. If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. Meaning depends on context: for checks it is the funding account; for ExpenseLineAdd it may be required by accounting preferences; for credit-card transactions it identifies the bank or card account involved. Different transaction types increase or decrease account balances accordingly.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

amount.description: The total of the amounts in the expense lines, item lines, and item group lines.

amount_in_home_currency.description: Amount in units of the home currency.

currency_ref.description: A currency record defines how QuickBooks stores and displays a currency. Built-in currency name/code values are fixed; formatting and active status can vary by settings and workflow.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

post.description: A credit card charge is a general charge incurred when a QuickBooks user makes a purchase using a credit card. put.description: The Credit Card charge mod request allows you to modify an existing credit card charge transaction using the SDK. You can modify most of the fields that can be modified in the QuickBooks UI. That is, this request can be used to modify Purchased from, date, credit card and modify lines from the item table and the expense table. The following list describes what you can and can’t due with this request: You can modify or clear the following fields: Ref Num and Memo You can modify (not clear) transaction date You can change the credit card account to support the scenario where the credit card transaction was created and posted to the wrong credit card account (impacts your accounting). You can modify the Purchase from field (Payee Name) to change the Payee Name on the credit card transaction to a different name (employee, job, customer, vendor, other name). This field can’t be cleared since it is required by QB business logic You can’t modify the amount due directly! (However the amount due will change when you modify the transaction lines.) You can’t change a Charge to a Credit. You can’t Void the charge. Use TxnVoid instead. You can clear the entire expense table or the entire item table, but you can’t clear both tables at the same time. The `credit_card_charge_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

sales_tax_code_ref.description: SalesTaxCodeRef points to the sales-tax code used for an item or customer context. QuickBooks includes default TAX and NON codes, and a code can be deleted only when nothing references it. If sales tax is disabled, QuickBooks assigns the default non-taxable code. If both FullName and ListID are provided in SalesTaxCodeRef, FullName is ignored.

txn_line_id.description: Identification number of the transaction line. (TxnLineID is supported as of v2.0 of the SDK. With qbXML v1.0 and v1.1, TxnLineID is always returned as zero.) If you need to add a new transaction line in a transaction Mod request, you can do so by setting the TxnLineID to -1.

unit_of_measure.description: In a transaction line item, the name of the unit of measure selected from within the item’s available units. If the company file is enabled only for single unit of measure per item, this must be the base unit!

override_uom_set_ref.description: When you modify a transaction line to change the unit of measure used in that line, you use this aggregate to specify the UOM set within which you are choosing an available unit of measure. The “override” here refers to the unit within the set, not the UOM Set itself, which you can’t change or override–the UOM set that can be set or changed only in the item itself via an Item Mod request.

quantity.description: On transaction lines, QuickBooks can derive one value from the other two among Quantity, Rate, and Amount. If you supply Quantity and Amount, QuickBooks calculates Rate. If you supply Quantity and Rate, QuickBooks calculates Amount.

total_amount.description: Total amount of money paid or received. In a receive payment add transaction that has payment amount elements (such as AppliedToTxnAdd lines) you must supply a TotalAmount and the sum of all the PaymentAmount elements must not be greater than the TotalAmount.

item_line_ret.description: An ItemLine is used to track any portion of a transaction that represents the purchase of an “item.” If ItemLineAdd doesn’t specify an Amount, Cost, or Quantity, then QuickBooks will calculate Amount based on a Quantity of 1 and the suggested Cost.

serial_number.description: The serial number of the asset.

lot_number.description: The lot number of the asset.

billable_status.description: The billing status of this item line or expense line.

class_ref.description: Use classes to categorize transactions (for example, by department, location, or work type). Class tracking is off by default in QuickBooks. A ClassRef points to one class; if both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. In InvoiceAdd, a header-level ClassRef is applied to line items unless you override or clear it on individual lines.

cost.description: If both Quantity and Amount are specified, QuickBooks will use them to calculate Cost. Likewise, if both Quantity and Cost are specified, QuickBooks will use them to calculate the total Amount.

customer_ref.description: CustomerRef identifies a customer or customer job. If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. In SalesReceipt and ReceivePayment, it identifies who receives credit. In TimeTracking, it identifies who the time can be billed to and is required in TimeTrackingAdd when IsBillable is true. In ExpenseLineAdd, if AccountRef is A/P, CustomerRef must be a vendor; otherwise it must be a customer.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

txn_date.description: The date of the charge. In some cases, if you leave TxnDate out of an -Add message, QuickBooks will prefill TxnDate with the date of the last-saved transaction of the same type.

external_guid.description: Allows for the attachment of a user defined GUID value.

message.description: QuickBooks' own status message, carried through when there is no data to show for an otherwise successful request (a query that matched nothing, say).

code.description: QuickBooks' own statusCode. The stable thing to branch on.

message.description: QuickBooks' own statusMessage.

type.description: A stable name for `code`, when QuBeSync recognises it. Absent otherwise: coverage widens over time, so treat this as a hint and branch on `code` if you need certainty.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs this same document to it once QuickBooks has answered (`state` `response_received` or `error`, `response_json` filled in). `links.self` returns it on demand.

get.description: A PreferencesQueryRq request message returns information about many of the preferences that the QuickBooks user has set in the company file. Preferences can’t be modified through the SDK, only through the QuickBooks user interface. Note: If you include an explicit end tag in a PreferencesQueryRq request, you will receive an error if there is any space between the opening tag and the end tag. The following table shows valid and invalid ways of constructing this request:Valid(no space between opening and closing tags) Valid(combined opening and closing tag) Invalid (space between opening and closing tags)

parameters.description: The connection (a customer's QuickBooks company file) this request is queued for.
parameters.name: connection_id

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand.
parameters.name: webhook_url

response_json.description: `null` until answered. Then QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer, in one of the two shapes below.

accounting_preferences.description: Accounting preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

closing_date.description: The company closing date set within the company file. (The QuickBooks Admin can assign a password restricting access to transactions that occurred before this date.)

is_assigning_journal_entry_numbers.description: If true, QuickBooks will automatically assign a number to each journal entry.

is_requiring_accounts.description: If IsRequiringAccounts is true, a transaction can’t be recorded in the user interface unless it is assigned to an account. (However, transactions affected by this preference always require an account to be specified when added through the SDK.)

is_using_account_numbers.description: If true, an account number can be recorded for new accounts. If you include an account number in AccountAdd object when this preference is false, the account number will still be set, but won’t be visible in the user interface.

is_using_audit_trail.description: If true, QuickBooks will log all transaction changes in the audit trail report. If false, QuickBooks logs only the most recent version of each transaction.

is_using_class_tracking.description: If true, QuickBooks will include a “Class” field on all transactions.

current_app_access_rights.description: CurrentAppAccessRights indicates whether auto-login has been allowed, the name of the auto-login user, and whether the application has been granted access to personal (sensitive) data.

automatic_login_user_name.description: If auto-login is allowed for this QuickBooks company file, AutomaticLoginUserName gives the user name that is allowed to use auto-login.

is_automatic_login_allowed.description: If IsAutomaticLoginAllowed is true, then applications can use auto-login to access this QuickBooks company file.

is_personal_data_access_allowed.description: If true, then access is allowed to personal (sensitive) data in this QuickBooks company file.

finance_charge_preferences.description: Preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set for how finance charges are assessed against customers for late payment. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

annual_interest_rate.description: The interest rate, set by the QuickBooks user, that QuickBooks will use to calculate finance charges. The default value is 0.

calculate_charges_from.description: This preference is set by the QuickBooks user. Unless they change the value within QuickBooks, it will be DueDate.

finance_charge_account_ref.description: Refers to the name of the account used to track finance charges that customers pay. This is usually an income account. In a request, if a FinanceChargeAccountRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

grace_period.description: The number of days before finance charges apply to customers’ overdue invoices. GracePeriod is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of 0.

is_assessing_for_overdue_charges.description: If true, finance charges are assessed on overdue finance charges. This preference is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of false. (Note that laws vary about whether a company can charge interest on overdue interest payments.)

is_marked_to_be_printed.description: If IsMarkedToBePrinted is true, all newly created finance-charge invoices will be marked “To be printed.” (This makes it easier for the QuickBooks user to print a selection of invoices all at once.) This preference is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value within QuickBooks of false. Whether IsMarkedToBePrinted is true or false in the FinanceChargePreferences aggregate, the QuickBooks user can still change this preference for each individual invoice.

min_finance_charge.description: The minimum finance charge that will be applied regardless of the amount overdue. MinFinanceCharge is set by the QuickBooks user, and has a default value (within QuickBooks) of 0.

items_and_inventory_preferences.description: This aggregate contains the current item inventory settings for this company file.

enhanced_inventory_receiving_enabled.description: Indicator whether the enanched inventory receiving is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

fifo_effective_date.description: Date that FIFO (First In, First Out) is used to calculate the value of inventory sold and on-hand for this company file.

fifo_enabled.description: Indicator whether FIFO (First In, First Out) to calculate the value of inventory sold and on-hand is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_barcode_enabled.description: Indicator whether barcode are enabled for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_rsb_enabled.description: Indicator whether the bin tracking is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_build_assembly_enabled.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for build assemblies in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_inventory_adjustment_enab.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for inventory adjustments in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_purchase_transactions_ena.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for purchase transactions in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_on_sales_transactions_enable.description: Indicator whether the serial or lot number tracking is turned on for sales transactions in this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_tracking_serial_or_lot_number.description: Indicator on whether the serial or lot number tracking is being tracked for this company file. IsTrackingSerialOrLotNumber may have one of the following values: None [DEFAULT], SerialNumber, LotNumber

jobs_and_estimates_preferences.description: Preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set about how to handle jobs and estimates. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

is_printing_items_with_zero_amounts.description: If true, line items with zero amounts will print on progress invoices. (IsPrintingItemsWithZeroAmounts isn’t relevant unless IsUsingProgressInvoices is true.)

is_using_estimates.description: If true, this user is set up to create estimates for jobs.

is_using_progress_invoicing.description: If true, the QuickBooks user can create an invoice for only a portion of an estimate.

multi_currency_preferences.description: This aggregate contains the current multi currency settings for this company file.

home_currency_ref.description: The currency that is set as the home currency for this company file. The home currency is normally the currency of the country where the business is physically located. Although a home currency other than US Dollars can be chosen for the home currency, certain QuickBooks convenience features are available only with a home currency of US Dollars, such as the ability to download via a button click in the UI the current exchange rates for all active currencies, which is supported only for home currency of USD–otherwise you’ll have to look up and add the exchange rates yourself. Also, Intuit services such as payroll and online banking won’t be available as these services are only available in US dollars. Currently, once the home currency has been set and used in any transaction, it can’t be changed.

If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

is_multi_currency_on.description: Indicates whether the multicurrency feature is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on. Currently, once multicurrency is turned on for a company file, it can’t be turned off.

multi_location_inventory_preferences.description: This aggregate contains the current multilocation inventory settings for this company file.

is_multi_location_inventory_available.description: Indicates whether the multilocation inventory feature is available for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

is_multi_location_inventory_enabled.description: Indicates whether the multilocation inventory feature is turned on for this company file. A value of true means it is turned on, a value of false means it isn’t turned on.

purchases_and_vendors_preferences.description: Preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set about how to handle purchases and vendors. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

days_bills_are_due.description: By default, bills are due this many days after receipt.

default_discount_account_ref.description: Refers to the account where vendor discounts are tracked. In a request, if a DefaultDiscountAccountRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

is_automatically_using_discounts.description: If true, QuickBooks will automatically apply available vendor discounts or credits to a bill that is being paid.

is_using_inventory.description: If IsUsingInventory is true, the inventory-related features of QuickBooks are available.

reports_preferences.description: Reporting preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set. The preferences returned through the SDK apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

aging_report_basis.description: “AgeFromDueDate” means that the overdue days shown in these reports will begin with the due date on the invoice. “AgeFromTransactionDate” means that the overdue days shown in these reports will begin with the date the transaction was created.

summary_report_basis.description: Indicates whether summary reports use cash-basis or accrual-basis bookkeeping.

sales_and_customers_preferences.description: Sales and customer preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file.

default_fob.description: Default FOB (site from which invoiced products are shipped).

default_markup.description: Default percentage that an inventory item will be marked up from its cost.

default_ship_method_ref.description: Will be used as the default value in all “Ship Via” fields. (Refers to an item on the ShipMethod list.) If a DefaultShipMethodRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

is_auto_applying_payments.description: If true, a customer’s payment will automatically be applied to the outstanding invoices for that customer, beginning with the oldest invoice.

is_tracking_reimbursed_expenses_as_incom.description: If true, an expense and the customer’s reiumbursement for that expense can be tracked in separate accounts.

price_levels.description: Price levels let you apply custom pricing rules for selected customers. Once assigned, QuickBooks uses those prices automatically on supported sales forms unless explicitly overridden.

is_rounding_sales_price_up.description: If true, amounts are rounded up to nearest whole dollar for fixed percentage price levels (not for per item price levels).

is_using_price_levels.description: If true, price levels have been turned on for the company file (under Sales and Customers preferences), which enables the creation and use of price levels.

sales_tax_preferences.description: Sales-tax preferences that the QuickBooks administrator has set. These preferences apply to all users who log into this QuickBooks company file. post.description: This request merges one list object into another list object of the same type. Currently you can merge customers/jobs, or vendors, or accounts. The consequence of the merge is that only the merge-to object remains. The merge-from object goes away and all transactions that reference that merge-from object now reference only the merge-to object. The request itself is very simple: you just need the ListID and EditSequence for the two objects to be merged. However, you may have to do some preliminary work on the objects themselves before the merge. For accounts, you must make sure they have the same AccountType, and must stop if they don’t. (You can’t change the AccountType!) You must also check the Sublevel of the two accounts and change one of them to match the other before, by making the ParentRef point to the same parent account or by getting rid of the ParentRef, if you need to set the Sublevel to 0. For customers, you must make sure only one of the customers/jobs has child jobs. If both have child jobs, you must move the jobs first to the merge-to customer or delete the jobs. You can only merge two list objects from a QuickBooks company file if the file is open in single-user mode. If the file is open in multiuser mode, your application will receive an error.

If you want complete control over the report content, you will be interested in both the custom summary report and the custom transaction detail report. Custom reports don’t make any assumptions about the data you are interested in–they require you to specify exactly what data you want included in the report. Your application has to select the row and column axes, and it controls the output using common customization parameters for dates and filters. For the custom transaction detail report, you must specify all the include columns for the transactions you want returned in the report. For these reports, you are also required to specify a date element a DateMacro or a custom date range).

put.description: About SalesOrPurchaseMod versus SalesAndPurchaseMod in an ItemServiceMod request: You can’t change the reimbursable status of a service item through the SDK. For example, if a service item is marked as non-reimbursable in QuickBooks, you can’t send a modify request that includes a SalesAndPurchaseMod aggregate. Similarly, if you send an ItemServiceAdd request that includes a SalesOrPurchase aggregate, you can’t later modify that item using a SalesAndPurchaseMod aggregate. Starting with qbXML spec 7.0, you can modify the various account references using the appropriate account reference aggregate and the matching Apply Account RefToExistingTxns boolean. You need to use the boolean when you change an account ref because the QuickBooks UI displays a prompt asking whether the change should apply to existing transactions or not. Specifying True for the boolean basically dismisses this with a “Yes” answer, allowing your changes to be made and changes any existing transactions that use the item with that AccountRef. Specifying “False” means that the mod won’t take affect if there are existing transactions. Setting this to “True” should be used with caution and normally only after some user has indicated that they want those changes made to all those existing transactions! If any affected transactions are protected by a closing date and password, the AccountRef changes won’t be made and so the Mod request will return an error without making the requested Mod. The `item_service_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

parameters.description: Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

post.description: Adds an item receipt transaction, which is a transaction entered in QuickBooks when a shipment is received from a vendor. If you use PurchaseOrders to order from the vendor, you can link the item receipt to purchase order to receive the items against the purchase orders to automatically update (and eventually close) the purchase orders. This linking also saves you having to re-create line items as they are pulled in automatically from the purchase order. You can do this linking only in the item receipt add, not in the mod. The `item_receipt_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

txn_number.description: An identifying number for this transaction.

vendor_ref.description: A vendor is any person or company from whom a small business owner buys goods and services. (Banks and tax agencies usually are included on the vendor list.) full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

post.description: Adds a sales-tax item, which is an item used to calculate a single sales tax that is collected at a specified rate and paid to a single agency. (Compare with the ItemSalesTaxGroupAdd message.) An ItemSalesTaxRef aggregate refers to an item on this list. In a request, if an ItemSalesTaxRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored. Taxes can be reflected in transaction line items The following information refers to invoices specifically, but it also applies to sales receipts. Generally its best to assign a tax item or tax group item to an invoice and allow QuickBooks to apply the same tax to all taxable items on the invoice. However in some situations multiple tax combinations are required, so this method doesn’t work. In this case one must use techniques to apply the taxes in the invoice itself as line items. Using lines to apply taxes isn’t always straight forward. When applying taxes as line items, only single tax items can be used, tax groups can only be used for the entire invoice. If you have multiple taxes which apply to all taxable items, and one or more other taxes that only apply to some of the items on an invoice its better to use a tax group which applies to the entire invoice for the taxes which applies to all taxable items and then apply the other taxes in the invoice itself. One applies a tax or tax group to an entire invoice by using the ItemSalesTaxRef aggregate. One can use subtotals to apply a single tax line to multiple items in an invoice, but the tax is only applied automatically for the first tax line after the subtotal line. Any other tax lines which need to be applied to the subtotal line must supply their own amount. If you don’t supply an amount the amount comes out as zero and the tax line is useless. When one does supply an amount, the amount of tax on the subtotal also shows up in the rate column for that tax line. There isn’t any way for the rate to show up as anything other than the amount of the tax. If you have a complicated tax situation where no single tax applies to all taxable items on the invoice, you must choose a zero percent tax to apply for the entire invoice. It is recommended to name such a tax item “Tax Calculated On Invoice” so that it’s clear that the tax isn’t being applied by QuickBooks on the entire invoice. The `item_sales_tax_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

get.description: In traditional accounting, transactions are entered into the general journal and categorized exclusively by account. In QuickBooks, most transactions can be categorized either by account or by type (invoice, check, and so on). For a few activities in QuickBooks, you must use the general journal directly, for example for recording depreciation. Notice that you must supply the credit line and a corresponding debit line in the same request. It won’t work to supply them in two distinct requests. You can supply as many credit lines and debit lines in one single request as you want so long as the total monetary amount from the credits equals the total monetary amount from the debits in that request. Finally, DO NOT supply negative sign for the monetary amounts. QuickBooks does that for you. If you do supply the negative sign amounts will add instead of cancel and you’ll get a runtime error. Querying for Condensed Transactions If you need the query to return condensed transactions, you can do this by using either an Entity or Account filter in the journal query request. Alternatively, you could use the The generic TransactionQuery, which can return condensed transactions.

parameters.description: Use the metaData attribute to control whether query responses include counts. Options are NoMetaData (default), MetaDataOnly (count only), and MetaDataAndResponseData (count plus objects). parameters.description: The iterator attribute provided with most query types also allows you to break down query results in smaller and more manageable chunks of data. An iterator results in responses that contain only the specified number of objects. Iterators are only valid for the application that starts them, and they are only valid for the current QuickBooks session.
parameters.name: iterator

parameters.description: Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: account_filter

parameters.description: Filters by the specified currency. Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.

parameters.description: An entity refers to a person on the QuickBooks Customer list, Vendor list, Employee list, or Other Names list. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). post.description: In versions 1.0 and 1.1, all debit lines in a JournalEntryAdd request had to appear first, followed by all credit lines. But in versions 2.0 and above, the debit and credit lines can be intermingled. A credit line can legally come first in thejournal entry add. In traditional accounting, transactions are entered into the general journal and categorized exclusively by account. In QuickBooks, most transactions can be categorized either by account or by type (invoice, check, and so on). For a few activities in QuickBooks, you must use the general journal directly, for example for recording depreciation. Notice that you must supply the credit line and a corresponding debit line in the same request. It won’t work to supply them in two distinct requests. You can supply as many credit lines and debit lines in one single request as you want so long as the total monetary amount from the credits equals the total monetary amount from the debits in that request. Finally, DO NOT supply negative sign for the monetary amounts. QuickBooks does that for you. If you do supply the negative sign amounts will add instead of cancel and you’ll get a runtime error. Querying for Condensed Transactions If you need the query to return condensed transactions, you can do this by using either an Entity or Account filter in the journal query request. Alternatively, you could use the The generic TransactionQuery, which can return condensed transactions. If the transaction is a home currency adjustment, QuickBooks will ignore the IsAmountsEnteredInHomeCurrency, CurrencyRef, and ExchangeRate elements. The `journal_entry_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

sales_tax_code_ref.description: SalesTaxCodeRef points to the sales-tax code used for an item or customer context. If both FullName and ListID are provided in SalesTaxCodeRef, FullName is ignored.

sales_tax_percentage.description: The percentage charged for sales tax.

is_paid.description: If IsPaid is true, this transaction has been paid.

ship_address_block.description: The address expressed as an address block of Addr1 through Addr5, depending on the number of lines in the original request that created the address.

is_tax_included.description: For future use with international versions of QuickBooks.

is_pending.description: If IsPending is set to true, the invoice hasn’t been completed. Pending sales might include unpaid orders, estimates, tracked hours that haven’t yet been billed, or sales of back-ordered items.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

post.description: An invoice records the amount owed by a customer who purchased goods or services but didn’t pay in full at the time of the sale. If full payment is received at the time of the sale, it is recorded as a sales receipt, not an invoice. In QuickBooks, invoices and estimates use similar fields, and an estimate can be converted into an invoice after the customer accepts the estimate. However, in the SDK, there is currently no ability to create an invoice directly from an estimate (you can’t link an invoice to an estimate). If you Add an invoice that has an inventory item on it, QB will automatically calculate COGS and post it to the COGS account. (The inventory item will need to be setup to post to the COGS account and must have a unit cost in it.) However, notice that such an InvoiceAdd has sales prices, not cost, so the Add isn’t impacting the cost of the item. The cost of the item is only affected by purchases (bills and item receipts) sales and inventory adjustments. The Life Cycle of Inventory Items and Effects of Sales and Purchases The value of inventory is set when an inventory item is created or bought. QuickBooks uses cost averaging and decreases the value of the inventory asset account at the price when the sale is recorded. So, lets say a company starts carrying widgets as inventory items. First the inventory item must be created in QuickBooks. If the widgets are already in inventory based on a purchase made that won’t be recorded in QuickBooks, the user or application would add the inventory item description along with the quantity on hand and the value (total purchase price) of the quantity on hand. If the purchase is to be recorded in QuickBooks the inventory item would be created with quantity and value of 0 (zero). Then a bill would be added to QB which would increase the inventory quantity and value. Lets say we bought 10 widgets for $100. QuickBooks would then consider each widget to be worth $10. The next day a customer buys 5 widgets for $20 each. A sales receipt or invoice is created for the purchase, the quantity of widgets is reduced by 5, to 5 and the value is reduced by $50 to $50. The inventory asset account is reduced by $50 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $100. It appears that widgets will be a big seller, so the small business owner goes out and buys 10 more widgets. However, the supplier has also noticed a widget buying trend, so he’s increased the price to $25 each. So now our quantity is increased from 5 to 15 and the value is increased from $50 to $300, so they are considered to be worth $20 each. After purchasing the widgets another customer decides to buy 10 widgets but the price has been raised to $50 each. After the sales receipt or invoice is entered, the inventory is reduced to 5 and the value is reduced to $100. The inventory asset account is reduced by $200 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $500. Taxes can be reflected in transaction line items The following information refers to invoices specifically, but it also applies to sales receipts. Generally its best to assign a tax item or tax group item to an invoice and allow QuickBooks to apply the same tax to all taxable items on the invoice. However in some situations multiple tax combinations are required, so this method doesn’t work. In this case one must use techniques to apply the taxes in the invoice itself as line items. Using lines to apply taxes isn’t always straight forward. When applying taxes as line items, only single tax items can be used, tax groups can only be used for the entire invoice. If you have multiple taxes which apply to all taxable items, and one or more other taxes that only apply to some of the items on an invoice its better to use a tax group which applies to the entire invoice for the taxes which applies to all taxable items and then apply the other taxes in the invoice itself. One applies a tax or tax group to an entire invoice by using the ItemSalesTaxRef aggregate. One can use subtotals to apply a single tax line to multiple items in an invoice, but the tax is only applied automatically for the first tax line after the subtotal line. Any other tax lines which need to be applied to the subtotal line must supply their own amount. If you don’t supply an amount the amount comes out as zero and the tax line is useless. When one does supply an amount, the amount of tax on the subtotal also shows up in the rate column for that tax line. There isn’t any way for the rate to show up as anything other than the amount of the tax. If you have a complicated tax situation where no single tax applies to all taxable items on the invoice, you must choose a zero percent tax to apply for the entire invoice. It is recommended to name such a tax item “Tax Calculated On Invoice” so that it’s clear that the tax isn’t being applied by QuickBooks on the entire invoice. The `invoice_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

get.description: Queries for the specified inventory item or set of items. Notice that certain modifications to the item can be caused by other transactions, such as ItemReceipts where the item’s on hand quantity is increased. Modifications through these transactions don’t result in changing the TimeModified stamp (only the Mod operation will do that), but those changes will be detected when you use the FromModifiedDate/ToModifiedDate filters in your query. Notice that you can’t get an inventory asset value from QuickBooks using this query. Instead, you need to use the General Summary Report query (which currently doesn’t include Assembly Items). Suppose you needed a way to search for the amount on hand of items that have had their amount changed since a certain date. Again, you wouldn’t use this query, but a GeneralDetailReportQuery that has its GeneralDetailReportType set to “InventoryValuationDetail.” This will tell you which items changed by how much. Also, suppose you wanted the on-hand quantity from QB as of a specific date. You would use a General Summary Report of the type Inventory Valuation Summary. (Again, this report doesn’t include Inventory Assemblies.)

post.description: Adds an inventory item. An inventory item is any merchandise or part that a business purchases, tracks as inventory, and then resells. In QuickBooks, information about an inventory item is grouped into three categories:Puchase Information includes PurchaseDesc, PurchaseCost, COGSAccountRef, and PrefVendorRef. Sales Information includes SalesDesc, SalesPrice, and SalesTaxCodeRef. Inventory Information includes AssetAccountRef, ReorderPoint, QuantityOnHand, TotalValue, and InventoryDate. The Life Cycle of Inventory Items and Effects of Sales and Purchases The value of inventory is set when an inventory item is created or bought. QuickBooks uses cost averaging and decreases the value of the inventory asset account at the price when the sale is recorded. So, lets say a company starts carrying widgets as inventory items. First the inventory item must be created in QuickBooks. If the widgets are already in inventory based on a purchase made that won’t be recorded in QuickBooks, the user or application would add the inventory item description along with the quantity on hand and the value (total purchase price) of the quantity on hand. If the purchase is to be recorded in QuickBooks the inventory item would be created with quantity and value of 0 (zero). Then a bill would be added to QB which would increase the inventory quantity and value. Lets say we bought 10 widgets for $100. QuickBooks would then consider each widget to be worth $10. The next day a customer buys 5 widgets for $20 each. A sales receipt or invoice is created for the purchase, the quantity of widgets is reduced by 5, to 5 and the value is reduced by $50 to $50. The inventory asset account is reduced by $50 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $100. It appears that widgets will be a big seller, so the small business owner goes out and buys 10 more widgets. However, the supplier has also noticed a widget buying trend, so he’s increased the price to $25 each. So now our quantity is increased from 5 to 15 and the value is increased from $50 to $300, so they are considered to be worth $20 each. After purchasing the widgets another customer decides to buy 10 widgets but the price has been raised to $50 each. After the sales receipt or invoice is entered, the inventory is reduced to 5 and the value is reduced to $100. The inventory asset account is reduced by $200 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $500. An ItemInventoryRef aggregate refers to an inventory item. In a request, if an ItemInventoryRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored. The `item_inventory_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

put.description: Modifies an inventory item. Starting with qbXML spec 7.0, you can modify the income account ref, using the IncomeAccountRef aggregate and the ApplyIncomeAccountRefToExistingTxns boolean. You need to use the ApplyIncomeAccountRefToExistingTxns boolean because the QuickBooks UI displays a prompt asking whether the change should apply to existing transactions or not. Specifying True for the boolean basically dismisses this with a “Yes” answer, allowing your changes to be made and changes any existing transactions that use the item with that AccountRef. Specifying “False” means that the mod won’t take affect if there are existing transactions. Setting this to “True” should be used with caution and normally only after some user has indicated that they want those changes made to all those existing transactions! If any affected transactions are protected by a closing date and password, the IncomeAccountRef changes won’t be made and so the Mod request will return an error without making the requested Mod. The Life Cycle of Inventory Items and Effects of Sales and Purchases The value of inventory is set when an inventory item is created or bought. QuickBooks uses cost averaging and decreases the value of the inventory asset account at the price when the sale is recorded. So, lets say a company starts carrying widgets as inventory items. First the inventory item must be created in QuickBooks. If the widgets are already in inventory based on a purchase made that won’t be recorded in QuickBooks, the user or application would add the inventory item description along with the quantity on hand and the value (total purchase price) of the quantity on hand. If the purchase is to be recorded in QuickBooks the inventory item would be created with quantity and value of 0 (zero). Then a bill would be added to QB which would increase the inventory quantity and value. Lets say we bought 10 widgets for $100. QuickBooks would then consider each widget to be worth $10. The next day a customer buys 5 widgets for $20 each. A sales receipt or invoice is created for the purchase, the quantity of widgets is reduced by 5, to 5 and the value is reduced by $50 to $50. The inventory asset account is reduced by $50 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $100. It appears that widgets will be a big seller, so the small business owner goes out and buys 10 more widgets. However, the supplier has also noticed a widget buying trend, so he’s increased the price to $25 each. So now our quantity is increased from 5 to 15 and the value is increased from $50 to $300, so they are considered to be worth $20 each. After purchasing the widgets another customer decides to buy 10 widgets but the price has been raised to $50 each. After the sales receipt or invoice is entered, the inventory is reduced to 5 and the value is reduced to $100. The inventory asset account is reduced by $200 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $500. The `item_inventory_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

get.description: This is a general query to search through all the items, of every type, in contrast to the type-specific queries such as ItemInventoryQuery, ItemOtherChargeQuery, and so forth. ItemQuery will return information about all the items that are set up in the QuickBooks file. However, if you want to find out if an inventory item has had its on hand quantity modified by other QB transactions (such as ItemReceipt), then you can’t use this query! You must use the ItemInventoryQuery instead. Notice that you can’t get an inventory asset value from QuickBooks using this query. Instead, you need to use the General Summary Report query (which currently doesn’t include Assembly Items). Suppose you needed a way to search for the amount on hand of items that have had their amount changed since a certain date. Again, you wouldn’t use this query, but a GeneralDetailReportQuery that has its GeneralDetailReportType set to “InventoryValuationDetail.” This will tell you which items changed by how much. Finally, suppose you wanted the on-hand quantity from QB as of a specific date. You would use a General Summary Report of the type Inventory Valuation Summary. (Again, this report doesn’t include Inventory Assemblies.)

item_inventory_ref.description: An inventory item is any merchandise or part that a business purchases, tracks as inventory, and then resells. In QuickBooks, information about an inventory item is grouped into three categories:Puchase Information includes PurchaseDesc, PurchaseCost, COGSAccountRef, and PrefVendorRef. Sales Information includes SalesDesc, SalesPrice, and SalesTaxCodeRef. Inventory Information includes AssetAccountRef, ReorderPoint, QuantityOnHand, TotalValue, and InventoryDate. The Life Cycle of Inventory Items and Effects of Sales and Purchases The value of inventory is set when an inventory item is created or bought. QuickBooks uses cost averaging and decreases the value of the inventory asset account at the price when the sale is recorded. So, lets say a company starts carrying widgets as inventory items. First the inventory item must be created in QuickBooks. If the widgets are already in inventory based on a purchase made that won’t be recorded in QuickBooks, the user or application would add the inventory item description along with the quantity on hand and the value (total purchase price) of the quantity on hand. If the purchase is to be recorded in QuickBooks the inventory item would be created with quantity and value of 0 (zero). Then a bill would be added to QB which would increase the inventory quantity and value. Lets say we bought 10 widgets for $100. QuickBooks would then consider each widget to be worth $10. The next day a customer buys 5 widgets for $20 each. A sales receipt or invoice is created for the purchase, the quantity of widgets is reduced by 5, to 5 and the value is reduced by $50 to $50. The inventory asset account is reduced by $50 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $100. It appears that widgets will be a big seller, so the small business owner goes out and buys 10 more widgets. However, the supplier has also noticed a widget buying trend, so he’s increased the price to $25 each. So now our quantity is increased from 5 to 15 and the value is increased from $50 to $300, so they are considered to be worth $20 each. After purchasing the widgets another customer decides to buy 10 widgets but the price has been raised to $50 each. After the sales receipt or invoice is entered, the inventory is reduced to 5 and the value is reduced to $100. The inventory asset account is reduced by $200 and the undeposited funds or accounts receivable account is increased by $500. An ItemInventoryRef aggregate refers to an inventory item. In a request, if an ItemInventoryRef aggregate includes both FullName and ListID, FullName will be ignored.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

parameters.description: Use the metaData attribute to control whether query responses include counts. Options are NoMetaData (default), MetaDataOnly (count only), and MetaDataAndResponseData (count plus objects). Counts are approximate and may vary slightly if records are created or deleted during processing.
parameters.name: meta_data

parameters.description: The iterator attribute provided with most query types also allows you to break down query results in smaller and more manageable chunks of data. An iterator results in responses that contain only the specified number of objects. Iterators are only valid for the application that starts them, and they are only valid for the current QuickBooks session.
parameters.name: iterator

parameters.description: Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: account_filter

parameters.description: Filters by the specified currency. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: currency_filter

parameters.description: An entity refers to a person on the QuickBooks Customer list, Vendor list, Employee list, or Other Names list. You can use an EntityQuery request to get information about all the entities that are set up in the QuickBooks file. In an ARRefundCreditCard query, this must be a customer/customer job. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: entity_filter

parameters.description: This filter allows you to omit line items from a query response to get a smaller result. The default value is false, so line items are omitted by default. Set IncludeLineItems to true to include line items in the response if you don’t mind getting a larger result.
parameters.name: include_line_items

parameters.description: If you set IncludeLinkedTxns to true, then the returned object will include a list of all the transactions linked to the queried object. (This list is similar to the History view of a transaction in the user interface, but not identical, as the SDK list contains only linked transactions, not items.) Each linked transaction will be represented by a LinkedTxn aggregate. If no linked transactions exist, no LinkedTxn aggregates will be returned.
parameters.name: include_linked_txns

parameters.description: Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the metaData query attribute.) If you include a MaxReturned value, it must be at least 1. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: max_returned

parameters.description: Filters according to the dates when transactions were last modified. The ModifiedDateRangeFilter aggregate isn’t required to contain any elements, but if it is empty, we recommend that you leave it out altogether. Note that the time portion of the FromModifiedDate and ToModifiedDate fields wasn’t supported in qbXML version 1.0 or 1.1. (To filter according to the dates when transactions were deleted, use a TxnDeletedQuery message.) response_json.description: `null` until answered. Then QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer, in one of the two shapes below.

account_ref.description: AccountRef points to an account in the company file. If both FullName and ListID are provided, FullName is ignored. Meaning depends on context: for checks it is the funding account; for ExpenseLineAdd it may be required by accounting preferences; for credit-card transactions it identifies the bank or card account involved. Different transaction types increase or decrease account balances accordingly.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

address.description: If an address request fails, some combination of address fields might be too long. In a Check, BillPaymentCheck, or SalesTaxPaymentCheck message, Address is the address that will print on the check.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

city.description: The city name in an address.

country.description: The country name in an address, or, in returned Host information (HostRet or HostInfo), the country for which this edition of QuickBooks was designed. (Possible values are US, CA, UK, and AU.)

note.description: In a BillAddress or ShipAddress aggregate, the Note field value is written at the bottom of the address in the form in which it appears, such as the invoice form.

postal_code.description: The postal code in an address.

state.description: The state name in an address.

address_block.description: The address expressed as an address block of Addr1 through Addr5, depending on the number of lines in the original request that created the address.

addr1.description: The first line of an address.

addr2.description: The second line of an address (if a second line is needed).

addr3.description: The third line of an address (if a third line is needed).

addr4.description: The fourth line of an address (if a fourth line is needed).

addr5.description: The fifth line of an address (if a fifth line is needed).

amount.description: The total of the amounts in the expense lines, item lines, and item group lines. If a CheckAdd request doesn’t specify an Amount, Cost, or Quantity, then QuickBooks will calculate the Amount based on a Quantity of 1 and the suggested Cost.

amount_in_home_currency.description: Amount in units of the home currency.

currency_ref.description: A currency record defines how QuickBooks stores and displays a currency. Built-in currency name/code values are fixed; formatting and active status can vary by settings and workflow.

full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

data_ext_name.description: The name of the data extension. If this is a custom field, DataExtName will be visible as a label in the QuickBooks user interface. Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

edit_sequence.description: EditSequence is a server-generated revision token. It changes each time the object is updated. To modify an existing object, you must send the current EditSequence. If your value is stale, the update is rejected to prevent overwriting newer changes.

exchange_rate.description: ExchangeRate is the rate from this currency to the company’s home currency at AsOfDate. parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand.

response_json.description: `null` until answered. Then QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer, in one of the two shapes below.

col_id.description: An identifying number that corresponds to the position of this column in the report. The columns are numbered from left to right, starting with 1.

col_type.description: The type of data that this column contains. ColType values are formatted types. (Returned ctPercent values, for example, will have digits after the decimal points, and ctAddr1 values will be strings.)

data_type.description: The data type: IDTYPE, STRTYPE, and so on.

num_col_title_rows.description: The number of rows to allocate for column titles. Although this number is usually 1, with some reports it is 2 or 3. (For an example of column titles that span multiple rows, look at a ProfitAndLossByJob report in QuickBooks.)

num_columns.description: The number of columns in the report.

num_rows.description: The number of rows in the report.

report_basis.description: If ReportBasis is rbCash, the report bases income and expenses on the dates when money changed hands.rbAccrual, the report bases income on the dates when customers were invoiced and bases expenses on the dates when bills were entered.rbNone, the report uses the default ReportBasis, which is either the QuickBooks Preference setting or the QuickBooks default for a given type of report. In a report response, the SDK returns rbNone for reports that don’t support ReportBasis. (The 1099 report, for example, has its own basis for generation.)

report_data.description: If the report contains any data, it is given row-by-row in a ReportData aggregate.

data_row.description: A data row contains the actual data for each column.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

subtotal_row.description: A row that contains a calculated subtotal of the data in all the rows since the last SubTotalRow and, usually, a single underline. There can be multiple SubTotalRow aggregates in a report.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

text_row.description: A text row contains only text and is used mainly for headings.

total_row.description: A row that contains a calculated total of all the data that has come before and a double underline. There will only be one TotalRow per report. If TotalRow doesn’t include any numerical values, the columns required to show the total values aren’t part of the report. These columns weren’t included when the report was customized.

row_data.description: RowData describes one row in the report.

row_number.description: The row number. Rows are numbered from top to bottom, starting with 1.

report_title.description: The main title for this report.

parameters.description: Use the metaData attribute to control whether query responses include counts. Options are NoMetaData (default), MetaDataOnly (count only), and MetaDataAndResponseData (count plus objects). Counts are approximate and may vary slightly if records are created or deleted during processing.
parameters.name: meta_data

parameters.description: The iterator attribute provided with most query types also allows you to break down query results in smaller and more manageable chunks of data. An iterator results in responses that contain only the specified number of objects. Iterators are only valid for the application that starts them, and they are only valid for the current QuickBooks session.
parameters.name: iterator

parameters.description: Used in filters to select list objects based on whether or not they are currently enabled for use by QuickBooks. The default value is asActiveOnly, which selects only list objects that are active. Choose only one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: active_status

parameters.description: Filters results to objects modified on or after this timestamp. Desktop QuickBooks supports 1970-01-01 through 2038-01-19T03:14:07; QBOE supports 1900-01-01T00:00:00 through 9999-12-31T00:00:00. If only a date is provided, time defaults to 00:00:00. In QBFC, use the asDateOnly parameter to control date-only versus date-time behavior. Choose only one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: from_modified_date

parameters.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive. Choose only one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: full_name

parameters.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName. Choose only one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: list_id

parameters.description: Limits the number of objects that a query returns. (To get a count of how many objects could possibly be returned, use the metaData query attribute.) If you include a MaxReturned value, it must be at least 1. Choose only one of: `list_id`, or `full_name`, or the set (`active_status`, `from_modified_date`, `max_returned`, `name_filter`, `name_range_filter`, `to_modified_date`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: max_returned

parameters.description: Filters according to the object’s Name. parameters.name: name_filter

parameters.description: Filters results to objects modified on or before this timestamp.
