credit_card_txn_info.description: Contains data from the credit card transaction used in the payment. This data originates from a previous qbmsXML credit card transaction. The data following the element CreditCardTxnInputInfo” data is the data from the original qbmsXML request. The “CreditCardTxnResultInfo” is the data from the original qbmsXML response.

credit_card_txn_input_info.description: This contains data originally supplied in the QBMS transaction request. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. Normally, special lower transaction fee rates apply when these cards are used and this field is filled out. If this field is left blank, then the usual (and higher) discount rate applies.

credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. You should save this value for any possible QBMS SDK transaction requests that need it, for example, CustomerCreditCardTxnVoidRq, or CustomerCreditCardCaptureRq. You should also save this transaction ID and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you are intending to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. It is returned from the transaction request and should be stored for subsequent transactions, such as using it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd, ReceivePaymentAdd, ARRefundCreditCard requests to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. This value is returned in the QBMS response to a QBMS transaction request, and must be subsequently supplied by your application in the QB SDK ReceivePaymentAdd or SalesReceiptAdd request.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

txn_authorization_time.description: Timestamp indicating the time in which the card processor authorized the transaction.

For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

commercial_card_code.description: This optional field is used only for Visa and Master Card commercial cards. There are three types of these cards: purchase, corporate, and business. credit_card_address.description: The address associated with this credit card.

credit_card_number.description: Credit-card number for this customer or this payment. Beginning with qbXML spec 6.0 and QuickBooks 2007, you must mask the credit card number with lower case “x” and no dashes. For example, xxxxxxxxxxxx1234.

credit_card_postal_code.description: The postal code associated with the address for this credit card.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

ship_date.description: The date when the product was, or will be, shipped.

credit_card_txn_type.description: Indicates the QBMS transaction from which the current transaction data originated, for example, Charge, Authorization, Capture, Refund, VoiceAuthorization, or Void.

expiration_month.description: The month when the credit card expires.

expiration_year.description: The year when the credit card expires.

name_on_card.description: The name on the customer’s credit card.

transaction_mode.description: Indicates whether this transaction came from a card swipe (tmCardPresent) or not (tmCardNotPresent).

credit_card_txn_result_info.description: This contains data returned in the QBMS transaction response. This information block shouldn’t be used in CreditMemo requests for QuickBooks 2007 and new versions. Instead, use the ARRefundCreditCard request.

authorization_code.description: The authorization code is returned from the credit card processor to indicate that the charge will be paid by the card issuer. In a voice authorization request (CustomerCreditCardVoiceAuthRq), the authorization code is supplied by the card issuer over the telephone.

avs_street.description: This field contains the value avssPass if the street address supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s address on file at the card issuer. It contains the value avssFail if there isn’t a match, or avssNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

avs_zip.description: This field contains the value avszPass if the customer postal ZIP code supplied in the transaction request matches the customer’s postal code recognized at the card issuer. It contains the value avszFail if there isn’t a match, or avszNotAvailable if the card issuer doesn’t support AVS. Note: This field was required in qbXML 4.1, but is optional in qbXML 5.0 and later.

card_security_code_match.description: This field contains the value Pass if the card security code supplied in the transaction request matches the card security code recognized for that credit card number at the card issuer. It contains the value Fail if there isn’t a match.

client_trans_id.description: This value is returned from QBMS transactions for future use by the QuickBooks Reconciliation feature.

credit_card_trans_id.description: This transaction ID is returned from the credit card processor. merchant_account_number.description: This is the QBMS account number of the merchant who is running the transaction using the customer’s credit card. payment_grouping_code.description: Internal code needed for the QuickBooks reconciliation feature, if integrating with QuickBooks. payment_status.description: Indicates payment processing status as known by QuickBooks/QBMS integration state. `psCompleted` indicates confirmed success; `psUnknown` indicates status could not be definitively confirmed.

recon_batch_id.description: This value is returned by QBMS from the transaction request, and is used internally by the QuickBooks/QBMS Recon (reconcile) feature. You should save this value without modification and include it in the QB SDK SalesReceiptAdd or ReceivePaymentAdd requests if you want to save the transaction data in QuickBooks.

result_code.description: This contains the status code returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

result_message.description: This contains the status message returned in the original QBMS transaction response.

txn_authorization_stamp.description: This value is used to support the credit card transaction Reconcile feature within QuickBooks.

parameters.description: Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Also because OwnerID and DataExtName together make the data extension unique, and because custom fields all have the same OwnerID of zero, the DataExtName must be a unique value among existing custom fields. In contrast, the DataExtName for private data extensions must be unique only for the specified OwnerID GUID.

data_ext_type.description: The field’s data type, which corresponds to a qbXML data type. In an IDataExtDefAdd request object, if this is a custom field, DataExtType must be detSTR255TYPE.

data_ext_value.description: The data in this field. The maximum length of DataExtValue will depend on the DataExtType of this data extension. For example, if DataExtType is STR255TYPE, the maximum length of DataExtValue is 255 characters. If DataExtType is STR1024TYPE, the maximum size of DataExtValue is 1KB.

owner_id.description: OwnerID identifies who owns the data extension. Use 0 for QuickBooks custom fields that appear in the UI, or use a GUID for private extensions owned by an app. Keep private GUIDs confidential unless you intentionally share extensions across apps. If you do share them, both apps must use the same OwnerID and DataExtName, because that pair uniquely identifies the extension.

desc.description: Description that appears on the purchase order for this line item.

is_print_items_in_group.description: If true, a list of this group’s individual items their amounts will appear on printed forms.

item_group_ref.description: ItemGroup objects represent items that are grouped together for fast entry, and an ItemGroupRef aggregate refers to one of these item groups. full_name.description: FullName (along with ListID) is a way to identify a list object. The FullName is the name prefixed by the names of each ancestor, for example Jones:Kitchen:Cabinets. FullName values aren’t case-sensitive.

list_id.description: ListID and FullName both identify a list object. QuickBooks assigns ListID when the object is created. ListID values are unique within a list type, not globally across all lists. If both FullName and ListID are supplied in a request, QuickBooks uses ListID and ignores FullName.

override_uom_set_ref.description: When you modify a transaction line to change the unit of measure used in that line, you use this aggregate to specify the UOM set within which you are choosing an available unit of measure. post.description: Adds a discount item. A discount item is a percentage or a fixed amount that will be subtracted from a total or subtotal. Items should be subtotaled (using an ItemSubtotal item) before a discount item is applied to them, because a discount only acts on the line that is directly above it. A discount item is different from a discount for early payment, which is represented as part of a StandardTerms object or DateDrivenTerms object. Note: When you specify an ItemDiscount item in any transaction (by using an ItemRef), don’t specify a Quantity in the transaction. If you do, you will receive an error. Be Sharp When Using Flat Discounts Flat rate discounts are treated VERY differently vs. percentage discounts. A percentage discount only applies to the line right above it, so all of the tax implications for discounts apply ONLY to that line (Note that the story gets more complicated here for group items, subtotal lines, etc). A flat rate discount applies to EVERY line that is recorded above the discount. Thus, the $10.00 off you see is applied equally to the $100.00 Nontaxable target and the $100.00 Taxable target. Thus, the sales tax for the 10.00 discount totals up to -$5.00. Therefore, for the desired behavior, the user must fill out the invoice like this: Item $100.00 Non Item $100.00 Tax Discount $20.00 Tax In this scenario, the $20.00 discount is properly distributed to be half taxed and half not taxed, so the taxable amount for the discount line is only -$10.00. The moral of the story: Non-Taxable Discounts are VERY dangerous. You should almost never use them unless discounts in your state are never applied to sales tax. The `item_discount_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

put.description: Modifies a discount item. Starting with qbXML spec 7.0, you can modify the account ref, using the AccountRef aggregate and the ApplyAccountRefToExistingTxns boolean. You need to use the ApplyAccountRefToExistingTxns boolean because the QuickBooks UI displays a prompt asking whether the change should apply to existing transactions or not. Specifying True for the boolean basically dismisses this with a “Yes” answer, allowing your changes to be made and changes any existing transactions that use the item with that AccountRef. Specifying “False” means that the mod won’t take affect if there are existing transactions. Setting this to “True” should be used with caution and normally only after some user has indicated that they want those changes made to all those existing transactions! If any affected transactions are protected by a closing date and password, the AccountRef changes won’t be made and so the Mod request will return an error without making the requested Mod. Be Sharp When Using Flat Discounts Flat rate discounts are treated VERY differently vs. percentage discounts. A percentage discount only applies to the line right above it, so all of the tax implications for discounts apply ONLY to that line (Note that the story gets more complicated here for group items, subtotal lines, etc). A flat rate discount applies to EVERY line that is recorded above the discount. Thus, the $10.00 off you see is applied equally to the $100.00 Nontaxable target and the $100.00 Taxable target. Thus, the sales tax for the 10.00 discount totals up to -$5.00. Therefore, for the desired behavior, the user must fill out the invoice like this: Item $100.00 Non Item $100.00 Tax Discount $20.00 Tax In this scenario, the $20.00 discount is properly distributed to be half taxed and half not taxed, so the taxable amount for the discount line is only -$10.00. The moral of the story: Non-Taxable Discounts are VERY dangerous. You should almost never use them unless discounts in your state are never applied to sales tax. The `item_discount_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

post.description: This request adds a time tracking transaction to QuickBooks, mirroring the time-tracking feature available in the QuickBooks UI. The time tracking feature allows a QuickBooks user to base payroll or invoices on time worked. You can add time-tracking information to any vendor, employee, or person on the Other Names list in QuickBooks. If IsBillable is set to true, both CustomerRef and ItemServiceRef are required. There is no link between an invoice and the time entries. However when you do the invoicing from QuickBooks, QuickBooks does mark the time entries as “billed.” If you don’t record the time entries as billed properly, then you get into a user workflow issue where everytime the user creates an invoice for a customer, QB pops up a dialog asking if they want to bill the unbilled time (which you already billed from your app). That’s why beginning with QB2007 and qbXML spec 6.0 we added support for the “BillableStatus” field and add TimeTrackingMod so that you can mark the time as billed when you create an invoice for it. The `time_tracking_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

put.description: Modifies a time tracking transaction. This allows you to modify time entry and mark time entered as billed. Applications using qbXML spec levels less than 6.0 aren’t able to Modify a time tracking transaction. However, those applications can achieve the results of a modify operation by deleting the time tracking transaction (using TxnDelRq) and then re-adding it with the desired values. You can do this only if no other downstream transactions have used that particular time tracking transaction. (Otherwise, the TxnDel request will fail.) This differs slightly from the UI, which allows these transactions to be edited directly. However, even in the UI, modifying a time tracking transaction doesn’t result in changes to any downstream transactions that use it. There is no link between an invoice and the time entries. However when you do the invoicing from QuickBooks, QuickBooks does mark the time entries as “billed.” If you don’t record the time entries as billed properly, then you get into a user workflow issue where everytime the user creates an invoice for a customer, QB pops up a dialog asking if they want to bill the unbilled time (which you already billed from your app). That’s why beginning with QB2007 and qbXML spec 6.0 we added support for the “BillableStatus” field and add TimeTrackingMod so that you can mark the time as billed when you create an invoice for it. The `time_tracking_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

parameters.description: Filters according to the account name or ListID. If the “Use account numbers” preference is enabled in the QuickBooks company file, you can specify an account number (instead of an account name) for FullName and get the account you’re looking for. But if numbers have been used as account names, confusion could arise. For example, if you queried for an account named 2050, and 2050 happened to be the account number of a totally different account, the query wouldn’t return what you asked for (the account named 2050), but instead would return the account with the account number 2050. This problem won’t happen if the “Use account numbers” preference is turned off in the QuickBooks file, orthe account name exactly matches the account number. (In this case, query would return the correct account either way.) To avoid this problem: don’t name an account using a number unless the number exactly matches the account’s account number. If an account name must contain a number that doesn’t match its own account number, have the QuickBooks user change the account’s name slightly, for example to 2050a. Choose only one of: `txn_id`, or `ref_number`, or `ref_number_case_sensitive`, or the set (`account_filter`, `currency_filter`, `entity_filter`, `max_returned`, `modified_date_range_filter`, `ref_number_filter`, `ref_number_range_filter`, `txn_date_range_filter`). Members of a set combine with each other, not with the other choices.
parameters.name: account_filter

parameters.description: Filters by the specified currency. 201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs this same document to it once QuickBooks has answered (`state` `response_received` or `error`, `response_json` filled in). `links.self` returns it on demand.

post.description: Adds a vendor credit. A vendor credit is also known as a “bill credit”. That is, it is a credit that a vendor owes you because you overpaid your bill, returned merchandise, or for some other reason. The VendorCredit is referenced in a BilPayment transaction, inside the SetCredit aggregate. A VendorCredit shouldn’t be confused with a Credit Memo, which is something you owe your customer and which is referenced in a ReceivePayment request. The `vendor_credit_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

put.description: Modifies a vendor credit. Be careful! If you modify ANY line item, you must fully re-construct the line item table as you want it because if you edit even a single line item, any line item that is NOT in the vendor credit mod will be omitted. For full details, see the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide (PDF, 9.6 MB) chapter on modifying and deleting transactions and list objects. A vendor credit is also known as a “bill credit”. That is, it is a credit that a vendor owes you because you overpaid your bill, returned merchandise, or for some other reason. The VendorCredit is referenced in a BilPayment transaction, inside the SetCredit aggregate. A VendorCredit shouldn’t be confused with a Credit Memo, which is something you owe your customer and which is referenced in a ReceivePayment request. The `vendor_credit_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

201.description: Queued for the connection's Web Connector. Pass `webhook_url` and QuBe Sync POSTs this same document to it once QuickBooks has answered (`state` `response_received` or `error`, `response_json` filled in). `links.self` returns it on demand.

get.description: The Job Reports category includes both summary and transaction detail reports. They can be customized only by date range, by column summarization, and by common filters. Some job reports require a customer:job reference in order to work

parameters.description: The connection (a customer's QuickBooks company file) this request is queued for.
parameters.name: connection_id

parameters.description: Set DisplayReport to true to display this report within the QuickBooks UI. (Default is false.) If you want the request to display the report without returning any data to your application, set the responseData attribute to includeNone.
parameters.name: display_report

parameters.description: The default value is false, which means that the report won’t include any subcolumn information. To include all available types of subcolumns for this report, set IncludeSubcolumns to true. The SDK won’t return subcolumn information for data that can be easily computed. (For example, the SDK doesn’t return the “percent of row” column.)
parameters.name: include_subcolumns

parameters.description: The type of job report.
parameters.name: job_report_type

parameters.description: Allows you to query for a specified account type or for specific list elements.
parameters.name: report_account_filter

parameters.description: Allows you to query for a specified class. Classes can be used to separate transactions into meaningful categories. (For example, transactions could be classified according to department, business location, or type of work.) In QuickBooks, class tracking is off by default.
parameters.name: report_class_filter

parameters.description: The time period covered by this report. Choose only one of: `report_period`, or `report_date_macro`.
parameters.name: report_date_macro

parameters.description: The level of detail to include in the report.
parameters.name: report_detail_level_filter

parameters.description: Allows you to query for a specified name type (customer, employee, vendor, or other) or query for specific list elements.
parameters.name: report_entity_filter

parameters.description: Allows you to query for a specified item type (for example, discount, inventory, or non-inventory) or query for specific list elements.
parameters.name: report_item_filter

parameters.description: Returns reports that were modified between these two dates (inclusive). The range of acceptable dates for both FromReportModifiedDate and ToReportModifiedDate is 1970-01-01 to 2038-01-19T03:14:07 (2038-01-18T19:14:07-08:00 PST). Choose only one of: `report_modified_date_range_filter`, or `report_modified_date_range_macro`.
parameters.name: report_modified_date_range_filter

parameters.description: The time period covered by this report. Choose only one of: `report_modified_date_range_filter`, or `report_modified_date_range_macro`.
parameters.name: report_modified_date_range_macro

parameters.description: If you omit both ToReportDate and FromReportDate, the report will cover the current fiscal year to date. Choose only one of: `report_period`, or `report_date_macro`.
parameters.name: report_period

parameters.description: Allows you to query for posting reports, non-posting reports, or reports that are either one.
parameters.name: report_posting_status_filter

parameters.description: Allows you to report on specific transaction types (for example, charge, check, deposit, or estimate).
parameters.name: report_txn_type_filter

parameters.description: SummarizeColumnsBy determines which data the report calculates and how the columns will be labeled across the top of the report. For example, if you set the value to scbTwoWeek, the report’s column labels might be “Feb 10-23, 02, ” “Feb 24-Mar9, 02, ” and so on.
parameters.name: summarize_columns_by

parameters.description: Where QuBe Sync POSTs the answered request (this same document with `response_json` filled in), signed with `X-QUBE-Signature`. Send one with every request: it is how answers are delivered. Optional only so a script can queue and look up `links.self` by hand.
parameters.name: webhook_url

response_json.description: `null` until answered. Then QuBe Sync's summary of QuickBooks' answer, in one of the two shapes below.

col_id.description: An identifying number that corresponds to the position of this column in the report. The columns are numbered from left to right, starting with 1.

col_type.description: The type of data that this column contains. ColType values are formatted types. (Returned ctPercent values, for example, will have digits after the decimal points, and ctAddr1 values will be strings.)

data_type.description: The data type: IDTYPE, STRTYPE, and so on.

num_col_title_rows.description: The number of rows to allocate for column titles. Although this number is usually 1, with some reports it is 2 or 3. (For an example of column titles that span multiple rows, look at a ProfitAndLossByJob report in QuickBooks.)

num_columns.description: The number of columns in the report.

num_rows.description: The number of rows in the report.

report_basis.description: If ReportBasis is rbCash, the report bases income and expenses on the dates when money changed hands.rbAccrual, the report bases income on the dates when customers were invoiced and bases expenses on the dates when bills were entered.rbNone, the report uses the default ReportBasis, which is either the QuickBooks Preference setting or the QuickBooks default for a given type of report. In a report response, the SDK returns rbNone for reports that don’t support ReportBasis. (The 1099 report, for example, has its own basis for generation.)

report_data.description: If the report contains any data, it is given row-by-row in a ReportData aggregate.

data_row.description: A data row contains the actual data for each column.

post.description: Adds a sales-tax group item, which is an item used for calculating two or more sales taxes grouped together and applied to the same sale. For example, local and state taxes could be tracked separately but applied to a sale as one tax. (Compare with the ItemSalesTaxAdd message.) Taxes can be reflected in transaction line items The following information refers to invoices specifically, but it also applies to sales receipts. Generally its best to assign a tax item or tax group item to an invoice and allow QuickBooks to apply the same tax to all taxable items on the invoice. However in some situations multiple tax combinations are required, so this method doesn’t work. In this case one must use techniques to apply the taxes in the invoice itself as line items. Using lines to apply taxes isn’t always straight forward. When applying taxes as line items, only single tax items can be used, tax groups can only be used for the entire invoice. If you have multiple taxes which apply to all taxable items, and one or more other taxes that only apply to some of the items on an invoice its better to use a tax group which applies to the entire invoice for the taxes which applies to all taxable items and then apply the other taxes in the invoice itself. One applies a tax or tax group to an entire invoice by using the ItemSalesTaxRef aggregate. One can use subtotals to apply a single tax line to multiple items in an invoice, but the tax is only applied automatically for the first tax line after the subtotal line. Any other tax lines which need to be applied to the subtotal line must supply their own amount. If you don’t supply an amount the amount comes out as zero and the tax line is useless. When one does supply an amount, the amount of tax on the subtotal also shows up in the rate column for that tax line. There isn’t any way for the rate to show up as anything other than the amount of the tax. If you have a complicated tax situation where no single tax applies to all taxable items on the invoice, you must choose a zero percent tax to apply for the entire invoice. It is recommended to name such a tax item “Tax Calculated On Invoice” so that it’s clear that the tax isn’t being applied by QuickBooks on the entire invoice. The `item_sales_tax_group_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

post.description: This request adds a data extension definition to the specified object type (e.g. Customer) so that extension data can be written to a particular object of that type (e.g., this customer, John Smith. A data extension definition must be created before data can be written to the data extension. Notice that a custom field data extension definition can be created either by using DataExtDefAdd or via the QuickBooks UI by the user specifying a custom field for an object. Only custom fields can be defined through the UI, however, not private data extensions. Via the SDK, you create a custom field definition by setting the OwnerID to 0. You create a private data definition by setting OwnerID to a GUID that only your application owns or shares with other applications. Custom fields are available and visible within the QuickBooks UI, whereas private data extensions are seen and used only by your own application or other applications that know the OwnerID GUID. Data is written to custom fields either via the SDK DataExtAdd/Mod requests or via the QuickBooks UI directly by the end user. Data is written to private data extensions only via the SDK DataExtAdd/Mod requests. You should be careful not to use private data extensions in transaction line items because queries won’t return that private data (use only custom fields on transaction line items). Notice that creating a custom field data extension definition for Customer and Item causes an automatic propagation of that definition to certain transaction objects. See “AssignToObject” for more details. A full description of this behavior and its usefulness is provided in the QB SDK Programmer’s Guide (PDF, 9.6 MB). DataExtDefAdd doesn’t cause any events to be generated. The `data_ext_def_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

post.description: Runs one fake Web Connector session against this connection immediately, and waits for it -- instead of waiting for the simulator's own poll interval. It stands for a person clicking Update Selected, so QuBe lets it through even while it is spacing out scheduled runs (QuickBooks unreachable). The one exception: right after a failed session, before QuBe has told the schedule when to run again, it can't be told apart from a scheduled run and answers `result: postponed` -- run it again to go ahead.

parameters.name: connection_id
parameters.description: The connection to act on.

200.description: One Web Connector session ran against the fake QuickBooks

retry_in.description: With `result: postponed`: QuickBooks couldn't be reached on the last tries, so QuBe asked the Web Connector to wait this many seconds before its next scheduled run.

503.description: The simulator's Web Connector process isn't running

tags.description: Creating and managing the connection (a customer's QuickBooks company file) that every request below is queued against. See the Onboarding guide.

tags.description: Listing the requests queued on a connection, and discarding one the app no longer wants. A `webhook_url` on each request is the integration path (see the Webhooks guide) -- this is for a dashboard, a script, or catching up after downtime.
